text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- In a move to curb the influx of illegal immigrants, the National Security Council has decided to impose tougher penalties, including whipping, on aliens and those responsible for bringing them into the country.
-- A single body to regulate privatised entities is being considered to ensure that privatisation will bring greater benefits.
-- The Cabinet has decided to allow the Michael Jackson concert as permission had already been granted to the promoters, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said.
-- Heavy downpours the last two days resulted in several landslips, the death of an 80-year old woman, floods and evacuations in three states.
-- Two bodies were found and two others rescued as the search continues for three more Royal Malaysian Air Force crew members of the Nuri helicopter which crashed into the sea on Wednesday.
